names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 15 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Βάρβαρος ο Μυροβλύτης», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 6. мај ст. ст., „Свети Варвар разбојник.“ Свети is no rank, and **разбојник — the robber — is not a rank word in any of the mappings this wave works from**: `honorific.js` does not compose it, it is not what the folder's `types` hold, and it is the one thing on the page that distinguishes him. **So it is kept, and keeping it is what holds this folder out of the fold with the day's other Barbarus**, the soldier-martyr whose own heading gives him the bare Варвар — the same move Папучар, Тарсанка, Боровски and Кијево-Печерски made on earlier days of this wave. The by-name the Greek page gives him, Μυροβλύτης the Myrrh-streamer, is nowhere on this page and was not imported; the myrrh is in the body's last sentence and not in the heading.

The heading of the calendar’s name link for 6 мая ст. ст., «Варвар Луканский, мч.», with the rank abbreviation left off. The day’s own line calls him only «Варвара, бывшего разбойника», so the epithet is the name link’s and not the line’s.

floruit.note: saint.gr dates the raid he took part in by a reign and gives no year of his own: «επέδραμε στη νότια Ήπειρο και την Αιτωλία επί των ημερών του αυτοκράτορα Μιχαήλ του Τραυλού (820 - 829 μ.Χ.)». The interval is that reign as the page prints it; the page says his ascesis ran on for years afterwards and gives it no end date.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 6 мая ст. ст. — «Мч. Варвара, бывшего разбойника (IX).»

attestations.note: The Russian keeps him on the same Julian day as the Serbian, 6 мая ст. ст., and the Greek on 15 Μαΐου new style, which is a different menologion number and not a style conversion; nothing was moved. The day line’s «(IX)» agrees with the `floruit` the folder already holds from saint.gr’s reign of Michael the Stammerer, so `dates` is unchanged. The two hymns the day page prints for a Варвар are his and not the soldier Barbarus’s: the kontakion is headed «мученика Варвара, бывшего разбойника» and is proper to him, calling him passion-bearer and naming the myrrh, and the troparion’s heading «мученика Варвара, бывшего» is the same epithet cut short in the source’s own markup. The troparion itself is the common of a martyr with his name set into it, as the same calendar sets other names into the same text, and the hymn’s source line says so. The calendar gives him the epithet «Луканский», which the day line does not, and the life puts his robbery in Greece and his relics in the monastery of Kellia in Thessaly near Larissa; no place was written into `locations`. azbyka.ru was not read. Read 8 October 2026.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Βάρβαρος ο Μυροβλύτης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 15 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **Two other days stand on the page and neither is taken as a feast here.** The page's own closing paragraph says that the local hagiology of the Metropolis of Aetolia and Akarnania and of Corfu calls him «Όσιος Βάρβαρος ο Πενταπολίτης» and keeps his memory «στις 23 Ιουνίου» — a local Greek second day, recorded here and not moved. And the second pair of synaxarion verses the page prints, «Ἦν Βάρβαρος μὲν δοῦλος ἐν γῇ σὺν πόνοις… Εἴκαδε ἠδὲ Τρίτη γε πέπαυται Βάρβαρος ἄθλων», sends the reader to the twenty-third and calls its Barbarus a slave, which this one was not: it is a verse for another man of the name and nothing on the page repeats it, so nobody is moved on it. **He is not the corpus's `barbarus-6-may`**, so far as either page can show: that folder holds doxologia.ro's «Sfântul Mucenic Varvar» of 6 mai, a martyr with no life, no country, no century and no hymn, while this is an Όσιος of Aetolia with a full life, a reign, a service and a myrrh-streaming tomb. The two are kept apart here and the question is left standing in the reader's report. **No relics list is printed** beyond the account of the 1571 translation.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 19.05.2026 (6. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети Варвар разбојник.“

attestations.note: **The day is Julian 6 May and the Greek keeps him on 15 Μαΐου, and that is not a conflict** — the Greek row was not moved, exactly as `silvanus-of-gaza` kept three calendars on 14 October beside a Serbian 4 May; and saint.gr's own page already reports a **third** day for him, 23 Ιουνίου, where the hagiology of Aetolia and Akarnania and of Corfu calls him Barbarus the Pentapolite. **The identification is the robber, the four-footed penance, the killing by mistake and the myrrh**, four things together: „После многих злочинстава покајао се“ against saint.gr's λῄσταρχος; „три године иде четвороношке“ against «πεποίηκε χρόνους τρεῖς κυλιόμενος ὡς τετράπους»; shot „помислише да је звер, а не човек“ against the farmer who killed him taking him for a wild animal; and „из његовог тела потече целебно миро“ against the myrrh-giving tomb that earned him the by-name Μυροβλύτης. **This is the day's second Barbarus and the pairing is what identified both**: the Prologue's „Свети мученик Варвар.“ is the soldier-martyr `barbarus-6-may`, upgraded in this same batch, and this heading's разбојник is the penitent. **NO DATE WAS TOUCHED**: this entry prints no year, no century and no reign, so the folder's `floruit` of 820–829 — saint.gr's bounds for Michael the Stammerer's reign — stands exactly as it was, and nothing was widened into it. New to the corpus from this page: that he **sentenced himself** to the penance in two parts, the second being **twelve years in the forest with no clothing, no roof and no food but grass and leaves**, which the Greek account has not at all; that **an angel brought him word that his sins were forgiven**; that his killers were **merchants shooting from a distance with bows** rather than one farmer; that **he asked them as he died to fetch the priest**, who came and buried him honourably; and that the myrrh flowed **from his body**, where saint.gr has it from the tomb. All four disagreements are recorded in the life and none is chosen. `types` was not touched: the heading carries no rank word — разбојник is not one — and the folder's `venerable` and `wonderworker` came from the Greek Όσιος and the myrrh. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Μαρτυρικὸν ἀγῶνα γενναίως ἠγώνισαι, ἀσκητικῷ δὲ πόνῳ τὸν βίον διήνυσας ὅσιε Βάρβαρε· διὸ τὴν χάριν ἐδέξω διπλῆν, διὰ μὲν τοῦ λειψάνου ἀσθενείας διώκων, τῇ ψυχῇ δὲ συγχαίρων τῷ Χριστῷ, ὃν δυσώπει, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τῶν αἰσίως τιμώντων σε.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ´, on the page of Όσιος Βάρβαρος ο Μυροβλύτης

english.text: Bravely you fought a martyr's contest, and in ascetic labour you finished your course, venerable Barbarus; and so you received a double grace, driving sicknesses away by your relics while your soul rejoices with Christ. Entreat him on behalf of us who honour you with gladness.

hymns.text: Τὸ σῶμα τὸ σὸν τῇ γῇ ὑποτίθεται, τὴν σὴν δὲ ψυχὴν ὁ κτίστης κομίζεται, καὶ τὸ μὲν ἀσθενέσιν ὑγείαν πᾶσι χαρίζεται, ἡ δὲ Χριστὸν ἱκετεύει λυτρώσασθαι, πυρὸς αἰωνίου τοὺς τιμῶντάς σε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β´, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν, on the page of Όσιος Βάρβαρος ο Μυροβλύτης

english.text: Your body is laid in the earth and your soul is taken up by its Maker; the one gives health to all the sick, and the other beseeches Christ to redeem from everlasting fire those who honour you.

hymns.text: Мученик Твой, Господи, Варвар,/ во страдании своем венец прият нетленный от Тебе, Бога нашего:/ имеяй бо крепость Твою,/ мучителей низложи,/ сокруши и демонов немощный дерзости./ Того молитвами/ спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 6 мая ст. ст., «Тропарь мученика Варвара, бывшего» — the heading is cut short in the source’s own markup for «бывшего разбойника», the epithet the kontakion beside it prints in full; the text is the common of a martyr with his name set into it, as the same calendar sets other names into the same text

english.text: Thy martyr Barbarus, O Lord, has received in his suffering an incorruptible crown from thee, our God; for having thy strength he cast down the persecutors and broke also the feeble insolence of the demons. By his prayers save our souls.

hymns.text: От Бога данныя ти благодати,/ страстотерпче Варваре святе,/ яко многоценным миром, нас посещай целебне,/ да вопием ти:/ радуйся, испивый сладостне чашу Христовых страстей.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 6 мая ст. ст., «Кондак мученика Варвара, бывшего разбойника», глас 3 — proper to him, and the heading that settles which Варвар of the day both hymns belong to

english.text: Out of the grace given thee by God, O holy passion-bearer Barbarus, visit us with healing as with myrrh of great price, that we may cry to thee: rejoice, thou who hast drunk sweetly of the cup of Christ's sufferings.
